prerequisites: Knowledge previously acquired in Physics, Mechanics, and Mathematics, specifically Elasticity, Plasticity, Strength of Materials, and Theory of Structures.
Ability to analytically solve isostatic or hyperstatic structures for obtaining force diagrams.
Understanding of stress and strain concepts and their relationship in elastic or plastic materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacities to apply the scientific and technological foundations of metallic structures.

teaching_methods: Autonomous student work, focusing on theoretical learning and problem-solving.
Reading and comprehension of basic bibliography.
Tutorial sessions (face-to-face when possible, and virtual).
Self-assessment activities, including solving self-check exercises and completing Continuous Assessment Tests.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.80 * Personal On-site Test (PP) grade + 0.20 * Continuous Assessment (PEC) grade. To have the PEC grade taken into account, the PP grade must be at least 4 out of 10. To pass the PP, a minimum of 30% of the assigned score must be achieved in each exercise. If continuous assessment is not chosen, the final grade will be solely the PP grade. PEC grades are considered for both ordinary and extraordinary exam calls.
